name: HheG-catalyzed ring-opening of cyclohexene oxide with NaOCN
description: Whole-cell biocatalytic ring-opening of cyclohexene oxide using halohydrin dehalogenase (IcHheG) from Ilumatobacter coccineus with sodium cyanate (NaOCN) as non-natural nucleophile in a two-phase system (ethyl acetate/water), scaled from analytical to pilot (10 L) scale. The reaction produces trans-hexahydro-2(3H)-benzoxazolone (trans-HBC).

identity.name: Halohydrin dehalogenase G (IcHheG)
catalyzed_reaction: SN2 ring-opening of cyclohexene oxide with NaOCN to form trans-hexahydro-2(3H)-benzoxazolone (trans-HBC)

reaction_components.notes: Screening: 20 mM; scale-up target: 200 mM (10x increase). Pilot scale: 0.48 kg in 50 L reactor.
2 equivalents relative to cyclohexene oxide. Non-natural nucleophile for ring-opening.
Main product. Isolated as white crystals after extraction with ethyl acetate and crystallization with heptane.
Co-solvent for two-phase reaction. Hydrolyzes in presence of NaOH, providing self-pH control at ~10.5. Also used for product extraction.
PB buffer, pH 7.0. Used in screening assay. Not needed in pilot-scale due to self-pH control by ethyl acetate hydrolysis.

operation_mode.notes: Batch reactions run for 16 hrs (screening/optimization) or 29 hrs (pilot scale) until target conversion reached.

reactor.notes: Screening: 96-well plates, 200 µL. Optimization: 10 mL glass vials, 5 mL reactions. Pilot: 50 L stirred tank reactor (Dongsen EXDS/JGRL), 10 L reaction volume.

multiphasic.notes: Two-phase system: aqueous phase (NaOCN, buffer/water, whole cells) + organic phase (ethyl acetate as co-solvent, 35% v/v). Two-phase system used to avoid direct contact of biocatalyst with hydrophobic/toxic cyclohexene oxide.

temperature.notes: Screening performed at 35°C. Scale-up and pilot at 25°C. Pilot scale showed exothermic phenomenon (>35°C); temperature controller used.

pH.notes: Self-regulated pH via hydrolysis of ethyl acetate converting NaOH by-product to ethanol and sodium acetate. Starting pH 7.0; endpoint 10.5 with ethyl acetate co-solvent. HheG active pH 7-11.

yield_and_conversion.notes: Screening hit (IcHheG): 42% yield at 20 mM cyclohexene oxide. Optimization (5 mL, 200 mM, ethyl acetate co-solvent): 95% yield. Pilot scale (10 L): 95% conversion, 87% isolated yield. Cell lysate showed 93% yield, comparable to whole cells.

selectivity.enantiomeric_excess: Only data from one experiment added
selectivity.stereoselectivity: trans-selective; nucleophile attacks back side of epoxide (SN2), leading to inversion at one carbon; symmetric substrate gives both (3R,7R)- and (3S,7S)-HBC enantiomers.
selectivity.regioselectivity: SN2 attack preferentially on tertiary carbons (C1 and C2) of cyclohexene oxide. Cyanate COM distances: 3.5 Å (C1) and 3.6 Å (C2).
selectivity.notes: ee = 53% at both 5 mL and 10 L scale. Previous literature reported ee 52% at 20 mM scale.

results.notes: Space-time yield improved from <2 g/L/24h (previous literature) to 25 g/L/24h.

preprocessing.treatment_procedure: Extraction with 600 µL ethyl acetate (screening) or 10 mL ethyl acetate (optimization). Organic phase diluted to 0-7 mM for GC analysis.

sampling.notes: Reaction mixture extracted with ethyl acetate. Organic phase analyzed by achiral GC (DB-1 column) and chiral GC (CP7502 column) on Agilent GC-6890N.

vessel.notes: 10 mL glass vials for co-solvent screening and optimization
Pilot-scale reactor; 10 L reaction volume. Temperature controlled by recycling cold water.
